I tried it too without the USB power and it still works well, but without the power, not all the channels came in.  For the little extra that this costs over cheaper antennas, it is worth it.  The long cord on it is a wonderful plus, as you can position it quite a distance from the TV, unlike cheaper antennas that may have shorter cords.  The only thing I can see wrong with this is that since it is powered, it does use some electricity, whereas cheaper antennas don't. Very satisfied with it and may get another one for other televisions in the house, once we cut off cable, which we are doing soon.  You recover your cost of the device with just one month of cable.  Extremely easy to install--under 5 minutes.

text_fidelity_a:
Koss SP540 Full Size Dynamic Headphones, Black with Silver Accents KOSS has created the perfect headphones for the amateur artist or the casual listener. They have put a great deal of work into both the functionality and aesthetics of this product. There are several things that I noticed at first glance:
(1) Aesthetics: The carrying case for the headphones is attractive. It is thin and practical. It fits well in a book bag, purse or travel bag. It does not take up a lot of room in whatever you chose to carry it in. The headphones fit inside the case nicely (face down), and there is a zippered pouch inside that holds the removable cord. The headphones themselves are sleek looking and attractive. They are black with just a splash of silver.
(2) Cool Feature: Making the cord removable was a great feature. Why? If you ever get a short in the cord, you have the option of simply ordering another cord without having to replace the entire unit. The length of the cord is fantastic....not too long, not too short. The only things that I would probably change about these headphones (although it doesn't affect my love of the product) is to include a volume control button and make the cord a little more decorative (maybe add a nice stripe of red..or something to add some bling). Ok that is just the girl in me.
(3) Fit: The ear muffs (or headphones) fit snuggly over the entire ear. They are nicely padded and comfortable. They do NOT cause irritation from prolonged use or press against the ear causing any discomfort.
(4) Sound quality: The sound quality of the KOSS is great or comparable, especially when I compare it to other sets that I have had in the past. They aren't bass heavy like Beats, but offer decent sound quality like Sennheiser, V-Moda or Sony. The balance and frequency response are good. No matter the type of music.. from Alternative, to Neo Soul, Jazz, Classical to Rock....I get great sound. I am very impressed by the quality.

And finally I will mention:
(5) Cost. This headset will cost you about $150, which is comparable to other headphones of this quality. I truly believe for the money, you are getting a pretty great buy. The sound quality and features make this a great set of headphones for those in the market to consider. You definitely get a lot of bang for your buck. 5 stars
text_fidelity_b: Koss SP540 Full Size Dynamic Headphones, Black with Silver Accents

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire E 15 E5-575-33BM 15.6-Inch Full HD Notebook (Intel Core i3-7100U Processor 7th Generation , 4GB DDR4, 1TB 5400RPM Hard Drive, Intel HD Graphics 620, Windows 10 Home), Obsidian Black I did a little homework and this machine, especially at the price looked excellent. I noticed in reading Amazon reviews that a small percentage of buyers had received machines with faulty screens. So I went to BestBuy to see what they had, and found nothing appealing in any where near this price. So I ordered one. It arrived on Wednesday (days matter in this little story). Knowing there was a slight risk, I opened everything very carefully, saved everything in case I'd want to return it. Sure enough I got one with a faulty screen. However I'd also calculated the odds: very slim chance of getting two in a row. Thursday we started what I thought was likely to be a tricky, time consuming effort: filling forms, emails, getting to UPS, etc etc. It went like this: one click to get to the trade request on the Amazon order, five minutes to complete it ....Including a stunning question: did I want to drop the first one at UPS, or have them pick it up at my door? UPS would have the prepaid return label with them.
Then they shipped the replacement to me Thursday. SAME DAY! Monday the new one arrived, the man had the return label in his hand.He took one look at my shipping ready packaged box, slapped the label on, and left while I watched still in disbelief. This is way beyond 5 stars for Amazon.

And true to the odds, this machine I'm using for this is flawless. I love it. It's everything it is advertised to be, and more. The slowness some mentioned was easily remedied for my use by clearing the "Start Up", using Blackle as a homepage, and one click to change the "Next Window" screen. I don't play complex games, just puzzles, solitaire and the like so no need for speed there. Pictures, movies and TV are all beautiful, and quick to load.

The Windows 10 Home is surprisingly user friendly...and I'm 72. The machine runs cool, easy to upgrade, and most of all: affordable. So don't be afraid to take a chance if you're waffling. Thank you Amazon! Very much.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire E 15 E5-575-33BM 15.6-Inch Full HD Notebook (Intel Core i3-7100U Processor 7th Generation , 4GB DDR4, 1TB 5400RPM Hard Drive, Intel HD Graphics 620, Windows 10 Home), Obsidian Black

text_fidelity_a:
iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair) My old G930 ear pads were flaking like crazy after several years of daily, all-day use, and I was hesitant to buy these at first because several people said they were too small. But I figured it's only $5, so it's worth a shot.

They arrived this morning and all I can think of is that whoever thought these were too tight or too small wasn't putting them on correctly. Maybe they thought they were just push-on instead of realizing that they have a flap (just like the ones that come with the headset) that needs to be lifted to go over the plastic part of the earpiece. That's what actually holds these things in place, people - otherwise they'd just fall off! Or maybe people aren't actually matching up the shape correctly. Either way - if you install them CORRECTLY, they fit perfectly.

These things are the correct size and I took some photos to compare the old Logitech-made pads with these. I also measured separately and they are the exact same size. If you take the time to look at how the original ear pads come off, you'll know exactly how to put these replacements on, and it'll take you all of about 10-15 seconds per ear pad.

These are virtually indistinguishable from the originals. I put these on and at first they seemed a little firmer than the original ear pads. However, I actually have a total of three G930 headsets (different purposes), so I was able to compare the feel of these ear pads to the original ear pads on one of the lesser-used, newer headsets. Again, pretty much identical - I guess they just get softer with use. Still, they are very comfortable even in their brand-new state, and I'm happy not to finish the day with black flakes on the sides of my face again.

PHOTOS:
I have three photos, two that are just comparing the back and front of the old pad to the replacement pad (and showing where the flap is that some people are apparently missing). The third photo is just showing the headset with one pad replaced so you can actually see that it looks pretty much the same as the original when installed correctly on the headset.
text_fidelity_b: iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair)

It was super easy to install and took less than two minutes. I cleaned my screen with a lens wipe first to ensure it was free of lint, finger prints and oils. Followed the included instructions exactly and lined up the screen protector with the Fire's camera etc and laid it down. The package had a stiff cardboard piece that works better than a credit card to smooth the protector sheet as you go - I have no air bubbles at all on the first try. Once it's in place, you need to remove the blue top layer to reveal the actual clear screen cover you will be looking at and touching when you use your tablet. The use of any screen cover is going to diminish the clarity of your high definition video, that's just a fact of life. This one is no exception. But...it does cut the glare in direct sunlight and it really helps prevent scratches to Fire's screen which means I can use my Fire in more places than before and in turn makes it more valuable to me. NETGEAR AC1200 Wi-Fi USB 3.0 Adapter for Desktop PC | Dual Band Wifi Stick for Wireless internet (A6210-100PAS) We have a router that supports the 802.11ac standard but until we got this router we had no way of connecting to it beyond the 802.11n standard. I was very interested in trying this adapter to see if it really is that much faster. It’s absolutely very fast and has wonderful connection reliability but suffers from a very slow software installation process.

I connected it to a Windows 7 64-bit system and allowed Windows to search for a driver. When that failed (as I assumed it would since this is a new product) I put in the installation CD and started the installer. The process took a surprisingly long time just to install and load the driver, to the point that I considered rebooting the box and starting over. It did finish though and then was ready to connect.

It connected without effort to our 5GHz network and immediately was able to serve up content. Everything seemed to be faster but we were not sure - until my teenage son connected to a Minecraft server and started playing. In addition to a lag-free connection he noticed about a 20% gain in frame rates sustained.

So far I can’t find anything beyond the clunky install that stands out as a negative. This is a fast adapter and it worth the one-time install time if you want fast, reliable connections and have a router that can handle the 802.11ac standard.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR AC1200 Wi-Fi USB 3.0 Adapter for Desktop PC | Dual Band Wifi Stick for Wireless internet (A6210-100PAS)

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS ZenBook UX303UA 13.3-Inch FHD Touchscreen Laptop, Intel Core i5, 8 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD, Windows 10 (64 bit) WOW! I've had this for about a month now and it is really great! Use this when I work from home or I am on the road. Blazing fast. Light as a feather. Easily connected to Bluetooth keyboard and mouse. The dongles work perfectly. At home I have extended the desktop to the ASUS IPS monitor - no problem. Sound is really good. I have not had any problem with the location of the power button or keyboard layout that other reviewers experienced. This is a great work-box for me. My 'work' computer was my HP Envy, which is a great laptop.......I find myself using the Zenbook more and more when working at home. This has also replaced my Samsung Galaxy Tab 10 as my 'mobile' tablet. So light and thin; easy to take with.

PROS
Super, super fast - this is the most responsive laptop I have ever owned
Incredibly light and thin - so portable, you will take it with you all the time.
super responsive keyboard & touchpad
touchpad auto-disconnects when Bluetooth mouse is enabled(sweeeeeeeet)
Easy to extend desktop with a VGA dongle
Connected Bluetooth devices perform perfectly - no drag at all
WIN10 is pre-installed

CONS
The power supply is a large, square 'plug' that covers at least 2 of the outlets on your surgestrip. Terrible design :-(
Dont buy if primary use will be Video streaming - glass screen is like a mirror/glare is a problem with video - difficult to find a video glare-free angle
There is a known WIN10 issue where pop-up dialog boxes are super-small and are extremely difficult to use. Microsoft is working on it
The first thing you should do is uninstall Macafee (pre-installed) - blocks so many apps., including Chrome (sigh)

UPDATE 03/29/2017
Just an FYI - I use this daily and love it, however I am now noticing the battery is getting hot after an hour or so of use. This is a new development. I am not sure what is causing this, but did want to share. I think I may have to shell out some cash for a new battery, which would be unfortunate. I have never had a laptop battery heat up like this before and have never had to replace a laptop battery. Not sure if others are having the same issue, over time.

My husband does not like hearing the speaker phone when he's trying to concentrate on his iPhone. It takes too much effort to talk on a speaker phone for hours. So as soon as I answer the phone I switch over to these headphones and talk through the microphone in the headphones. Perfect!

My friend who calls me once a week sounds like a radio DJ, in fact he used to be one but the headphones make him sound that way just naturally. It is really cute. He's always had a nice voice but this makes him come through like rich stereo sound. At first I thought I was talking to a stranger, but got used to his new voice sound.

So if you are finished with the headset you just press the middle button and it tells you the headset is off. So that saves on battery power and makes it easy to know when the power is on or off. I find that I can make these the best volume easily and have it now where I don't need to change it at all.

My friend who calls me every week told me about these headphones and I bought them on his recommendation. I had these years before I got an iPhone because I prepare ahead of time!!!! Now that I have a new iPhone 14 I'm happy as can be with my headset. Since the microphone is built in this is perfect for phone calls but it also works like a regular headphone if you want to listen to audio on your phone. I haven't started listening to music on it yet but will report back when I do. The sound is just superior to any headphones besides my AKG K553s.

~The Rebecca Review

text_fidelity_a:
Betron EMR90 Foldable Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over Ear with Microphone Mic Deep Bass There are fortunately many wireless headphones in this price range these days. Usually they are pretty similar, but this is one of the better ones. The first thing I noticed is how SOFT the ear cups are. It feels like something that belongs on a more expensive set, almost luxurious. That makes these much more comfortable to wear for long periods versus many of the other inexpensive headphones. The build quality feels good, and the sound quality is pretty decent too. Speakers of this size are usually pretty good at their bass response, and these are no exception. They naturally have a bit of noise isolation due to the cup design, and you have the option to connect a 3.5mm cable to use them as traditional wired headphones as well.
The one thing I DON'T like, is the microphone. Don't buy these for phone calls. The mic is too far from your mouth to separate you from background noises. Yes, I know airpods also have their mic far from your math but Apple has some sort of magic voodoo to make that work somehow. I've never liked the mic on any of these headphones, so I'm used to that by now. But I feel like these are marketed more for people who want to listen to music, and for that they are great and comfortable! I honestly wish they would disable the handsfree profile so that my phone wouldn't keep trying to use it for phone calls. Otherwise, a solid buy for this price!
text_fidelity_b: Betron EMR90 Foldable Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over Ear with Microphone Mic Deep Bass

text_fidelity_a: PHILIPS Fidelio X2HR Over-Ear Open-Air Headphone 50mm Drivers- Black I’m an IEM guy. I looked at some of my go-to Utoob channels for some direction and these were rec’d by many of those whose advice has been valid in previous purchasing decisions. Zeo’s was pretty stoked on these and the “Black Friday” price below $120 was a clincher. Once again my “friends” were spot on. They are comfortable (once I got a pair of wire rimmed reading glasses). The memory foam microfiber covered pads are good for hours of listening. The sound rivals some of my IEM’s although I find the soundstage to be a bit more compressed. The bass is definitely more defined but that seems to come at the expense of the highs although not in a bad way. I can see why the bass heads are crazy about these. The 35 ohm is comparable with all my devices including the cheap ass headphone jack on my ROKU remote. I did ditch the stock cable for a 1.5M SKS because I don’t require the 12’ cable that came with the cans, although it’s a nice cable. I do see a headphone amp in my future, perhaps the Little Bear B-4X portable tube amp. Lord save me from this addiction 😀

text_fidelity_a:
Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding I bought this at another website thanks to a Christmas gift card, but I researched the different types of sound bars and enhancement systems on Amazon & various places first. I wanted a very simple to use, unobtrusive setup, a digital connection and something that could work with our very open and large room without requiring setting up ugly components everywhere and still sound clean. This Denon base ticks every box for me.

I literally had this unit out of the box, installed under our 50" television, connected and working in less than 20 minutes - that includes reading the directions and unpacking. The box looked huge at first just sitting there alone, but once the tv was on top of it, it sort of vanished. Another 5 minutes and I had the Denon machine trained to respond to the volume buttons on my cable remote control. Mine came with a remote control, the digital optical cable and the red & white style connection. It connected to my phone and tablet via Bluetooth on the first try and played music through both using the Amazon Prime streaming and music saved to my devices - the sound is excellent by the way.

The included remote is handy for switching between daytime and night modes - the overall sound is lower in night mode. And you can choose between the surround sound mode or regular with the remote as well. One thing I have noticed, is that it can take three to five seconds for those changes to register and to hear them. The box turns on automatically when it senses a signal - no need to fiddle with it. Just turn the tv on & go about your business like always. The most impressive thing here is the improvement in the quality of the sound - every single bit is better! The guy reporting the news, music channels, background sound effects in movies, conversations in dramas... it's all crisp and clear and full. I am really pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding

text_fidelity_a:
Native Union Night Cable - 10ft Ultra-Strong Reinforced [MFi Certified] Durable Lightning to USB-A Charging Cable with Weighted Knot Compatible with for iPhone 14, iPhone 13 and Earlier (Cosmos) There are two of us in the house that use iPhones with the lightning port and as such we do need extra cables. Lightning cables are great but they do have a tendency to break. Also, not all third-party cables are the same and some are not worth the box they ship in. I was anxious to try this cable and I have found it to be a perfectly acceptable replacement for the one that came with my phone. Actually, it’s better.

First things first - it is important to note that this cable is MFI-certified which is actually a big deal. I have worked with cables that are certified and those that are not. Those that carry certification are guaranteed to work properly with your device, while those that are not certified are a roll of the dice. This cable is certified so it means two things you can expect from it: it will allow you to charge your phone without worry, and it will allow you to connect your phone to your computer without complaining about the cable being unauthorized. It just works.

The cable is shielded in a heavy nylon weave and that is a double-edged sword. On one hand it means the cable is very stiff and not very bendy which may or may not be an issue. More importantly, though, it means it is going to last longer than plastic coated cables which tend to flex and break.

The ends are terminated well too, with a hard plastic sleeve at the end of each plug where the cable connects. This spot is where most cables fail, and it is nice to see that some thought was put into reinforcing the cable at this point.

The weighted ball is interesting but to me it gets in the way. It can be slid up and down the cable which has its uses, but it is large enough and bulky enough to be more of a hindrance to me than a help. That said, if you are putting this cable in an area where it will not be moved and you intend to leave it there for the long term, it does prevent tangles and it allows for keeping gently tension on the cable.

Overall, I am pleased with this cable. It’s a lot less expensive than Apple-branded cables and it definitely is more durable and should last a long time.
text_fidelity_b: Native Union Night Cable - 10ft Ultra-Strong Reinforced [MFi Certified] Durable Lightning to USB-A Charging Cable with Weighted Knot Compatible with for iPhone 14, iPhone 13 and Earlier (Cosmos)

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input This unit is large and not at all like the dimensions listed on Amazon. It is 5 inches high (top to bottom), 8 inches deep (front to back), and 16 inches in long (side-to-side).

WHAT COMES IN THE BOX:
- one speaker unit with both left and right speakers inside the large housing
- one power cord
- one FM antenna cord / wire
- one AAA battery
- one remote
- three user guides; one in English, Spanish, and French (I love this because I can keep the instructions in English and throw out the others)
- one limited 1-year warranty insert

FEATURES:
- Bluetooth speaker
- CD player
- FM Radio with ability for 30 preset radio stations
- Ability to operate controls via remote or front of the unit buttons
- Clock
- Sleep / timer function up to 120 minutes in 15-minute increments
- LED Dimmer
- USB terminal that supports USB memory (thumb drive) in FAT 16 or FAT 32 format
- Line In port to plug in an external audio device such as earphones / headphones

The sound this produces when I play my CDs was awesome and music to my ears. I also paired this speaker with my Google Nexus 7 Tablet (2013 version Android device) and my iPad Pro 12.9 and experienced moderately powerful sound there as well. The FM radio was staticky but that was due to the location of where I placed my unit. When I did receive a station, the sound was great.

In summary, this produces beautiful sound. As a Bluetooth speaker, it does not produce as powerful a sound as my [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Block Rocker]] but it is still good. The addition of the FM radio is a nice touch. I also like that it functions as an LED clock. The instructions and operation of the unit take a bit of getting use to and can be confusing but I was eventually able to figure it out; although I may have to consult the pamphlet every now and then. Overall, this is a well-rounded unit for indoor use but the unit is larger than I expected. It is as large as those old AM/FM amplifiers from years ago and has a retro 70’s look (see attached picture).

PS For those who are interested in comparisons, this is my sixth Bluetooth speaker. I ordered five other Bluetooth speakers over a several year period. I have a [[ASIN:B007ZG03DG Bose Wave Bluetooth Music Adapter]], which is not very good and a [[ASIN:B00MPMK3GW Goal Zero 94014 Rock Out 2 Green Solar Rechargeable Speaker]] which does not work when paired with some devices and, when it does pair well, it usually lacks the powerful sound I am looking for.

I also purchased one [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Audio Block Rocker (iPA76A) | Portable Bluetooth Speaker]] and one [[ASIN:B01N17AQ7U ION Audio IPA88 Tailgater Flash Wireless/Bluetooth Speaker]] both from Costco. I absolutely love the Block Rocker (except for when paired with my iPad Pro) and I only like the Tailgate Flash. The lights on the Tailgate Flash annoy me because they have to be turned off every time I power on the unit. Nevertheless, the sound from the ION speakers are usually awesome. The IONs are the only ones I use frequently indoors (even though they are more of an outdoor Bluetooth speaker). They are battery powered powerful speakers and the sound is intense. If one wants Bluetooth only with the capability of travelling with them without having to find a power outlet, then these are worth considering.

I also have a [[ASIN:B01MUG5WIN Sony XB20 Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth, Blue (2017 model)]] which pairs well with my HP Omen Laptop and moderately well with my Nexus 7 and iPad Pro. However, this has to be charged first just like the Goal Zero speaker that I dislike.

PS My boyfriend connected his iPad 3 to this one's Bluetooth and loves it for listening to Podcasts. In order to get the volume as loud as he wanted, he also used the volume controls on the side of his iPad in conjunction with the volume knob on the Toshiba. On another note, he mentioned that the controls located below the CD player are very small for someone who has eye problems and I would agree with that. What I find inconvenient is that the button to open and close the CD player is there so that when the CD is open, I have to put my hand underneath it to close if I am not using the remote. Nevertheless, he loves this Toshiba just like I do.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input

My older set up is more adjustable. I can set the iPad at a different angle - easily - for typing on my lap versus typing on a desk versus typing on a table. I think this one is supposed to be more adjustable, but it's stiff and feels like it will break if I try to force it.

text_fidelity_a:
B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography I am best described as a skilled amateur when it comes to photography and I am always looking for ways to get better and to build my knowledge and ability. I am not a professional by any means, but I know a lot more than the average selfie-taker. I have wanted a ring light for a little while and I was delighted to have the chance to get to use this one. It does work, in the right circumstances, but it is definitely aimed at the base consumer market and is priced accordingly.

Thought it can be used as part of a professional set-up, it is designed and marketed as a consumer-grade unit. There are a number of obvious design decisions that make this more than just a little apparent. The tripod is good, but the mounts are designed for smartphones and will not work for DSLR cameras, mirrorless cameras or video cameras. That’s ok, as it is clearly marketed that way. The unit uses a USB power source which is an important point – the light itself isn’t especially bright like one that uses a normal AC power source. To be effective, the light needs to be fairly close to the subject. If a dim directional light is needed, a regular desk lamp is more than adequate in most cases. The upshot is that using USB power makes it much more portable for travel (more on that in a moment).

The remote allows for making a few adjustments to the light itself. There are three color modes and ten brightness modes, all of which can be (rather, must be) set through the remote. The adjustments are sufficient for this grade of light, though I would have found more colors and a more smooth graduation in brightness to be more useful. That’s more of a nitpick than a criticism considering the price point.

Build-wise, this unit is acceptable. It should hold up well enough in the studio or home office. What is lacking is a carry case to protect it when travelling. Considering the target audience (social media producers), this is an oversight that I think is important. To transport this light, it should be well secured and the only recourse as sold is to put it back in the original box, and that’s just unwieldy. Plan accordingly if you choose to transport this light.

This is an adequate unit for its target audience but will leave the aspiring professional underwhelmed. If you are looking for something that will work sufficiently for making posts to social media this is a reasonable unit; if you need a serious ring light for photography, consider other options. text_fidelity_a:
Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System First, I have to say, these sound amazing for their size, picking up even most low frequencies. Crank them up, and they almost vibrate themselves off the table - you can feel the bass just by putting your hand in the open air behind them. I can say confidently that these sound better than the old Boston Acoustics computer speakers that included a small subwoofer.

They are also good looking, have a standard auxiliary input in the back for versatility, and have a headphone output in the front (still trying to figure out when that could come in handy...) They also connect easily to my BB 9700, Xoom, and Win7 PC. Surprisingly, I can even control the volume from the speakers or from the controlling device!

The one speaker has a ~1.5m cable permanently attached that ends in an RCA plug that must be plugged into the other speaker. That can be extended, of course, but somehow, this makes the whole wireless thing less impressive. Somehow, I'd like to have them both pick up Bluetooth separately, but then of course, both would need separate power supplies and receptacles. The point is, for installations such as a home computer setup, what is the point of going Bluetooth for speakers? On the other hand, it is super cool to be able to just spit music from your phone at any time.

My other qualm is that they should have grill covers; I tend to pick them both up with one hand and have to be a bit careful not to stick my finger through the cone.

Overall, I'm impressed with the technology and the product itself. If you have a good use for this particular type of product and can deal without grill covers, I'm sure you'll be happy with the purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System

text_fidelity_a:
iCrius Reading Light for Bed, Table Lamps for Bedroom, Dimmable LED Desk Lamp I received this as a free review sample. It is close to being perfect, but there is one thing that prevented me from awarding it five stars: the power cable is hardwired into the lamp. It's basically a standard USB cable that should have been a standard USB micro or USB C style, but is instead unremovable from the lamp. That means that if you damage the cable instead of replacing it with a readily available USB cable the repair cost is probably greater than replacing the entire lamp - unless you are handy at such things.

Aside from the cable, I love this lamp. For one thing the clamp will firmly hold the entire lamp in place on a music stand's thin, metal shelf. Plus the gooseneck, while flexible,holds the lamp where you place it. I have similar lamp that will move position if you bump it, so for me this one is vastly better than most.

I do love the fact that I can power this from a wall using the included charging adapter or from a battery such as a [[ASIN:B014O2AXB0 Kikicom Power Bank]] (or similar model). Also you can actually power it from a laptop's USB port, which makes it perfect for small study desks. The included charger has a 1 Amp port for powering the lamp and a port marked 2.1 Amps for charging phones and tablets. To be honest, the 2.1 port is not especially fast and I suspect outputs less than the labeled capacity, but it still can keep up with my tablet.

Bottom line: if you area musician this is possibly the best music stand lamp in its price range (and it is not described as a music stand lamp!) For reading and even small room lighting it is also excellent. It would be an easy five stars had the cable been standard.
text_fidelity_b: iCrius Reading Light for Bed, Table Lamps for Bedroom, Dimmable LED Desk Lamp

XSKN Mac OS X Shortcut Silicone US and EU Common Version Keyboard Skin Cover for 2015 and Before 2015 Released MacBook Air Pro 13 15 17 Inch A1278 A1286 A1297 A1342 A1369 A1398 A1425 A1466 A1502 A1314 I used to be able to type 140 words per minute when I was a typographer. The key to speeds like that is not looking at the keyboard, ever. When I received this keyboard skin (in return for my honest review) and put it on my MacBook Pro 15" Retina, I realized why my typing speed has slowed down so much. It's because I always seem to be looking at the keyboard! And having this skin on made me have to unlearn this bad behavior. Now I'm trying to look at it only when I can't remember a keyboard shortcut and need to refer to the key tops for instructions. This is like mini flashcards, a proven learning tool.

Once I got used to how different it is not to be looking at the keyboard all the time, I'm now getting used to the slightly different feel of typing on the skin. It's really a subtle difference. The skin fits exceptionally well, and it's great to know I'm not getting dust and dog hair floating into the keys; also, I don't have to worry quite so much about spilling coffee into the keyboard. I'm also bad about being heavy-handed enough to literally wear the type off the keys, so I know this will protect my laptop from that.

Of course, some keystroke combinations are already second nature to me: Cmd-C, Cmd-V, Cmd-S. But I forget most of the others, so this particular skin is great for me to finish learning the shortcuts. But now, what I really, really, really want, is skins for Serif's award-winning Affinity Designer (Illustrator competitor) and their new Affinity Photo (Photoshop competitor). Please, Lifepersuit, give us skins for these!

One thing to be aware of: Look at the video review elsewhere by the guy who keeps these skins in their package to use as quick-learning guides. I didn't realize it when I receive my skin in a clamshell package that I didn't have to cut the package apart to get the skin out. But—duh!—the package has a tabbed perforation on the back that pulls open easily and can be pressed closed again. So I could have taken my skin out, then if I wanted to use a different skin, I could have stored the skin back in its original package. The package has a hanging hole, so it can be hung on a hook. I wish I hadn't screwed up my original package by cutting it open!
text_fidelity_b: XSKN Mac OS X Shortcut Silicone US and EU Common Version Keyboard Skin Cover for 2015 and Before 2015 Released MacBook Air Pro 13 15 17 Inch A1278 A1286 A1297 A1342 A1369 A1398 A1425 A1466 A1502 A1314

This Intel Core i3-based laptop is astonishingly, agonizingly slow. I bought this to replace a 7 year-old MacBook Pro that had served well, but didn't have the horsepower to run the latest version of OS X. This Acer is only marginally faster than the MacBook, and feels slower in may respects. It's glacially sluggish to start-up or restart, and Excel and Word crawl along at speeds reminiscent of 1980s era PCs. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.
text_fidelity_b: eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert

PROS of this product
* Easy to set up and use.
* Quality of the sound is good and it isn't heavy on the bass. Music is clear. The one speaker (mono) gives off great sound.
*Item is portable and sturdy.
*Item has Bluetooth function or you can hook it straight to your device. (I used my son's cord from his VModa head-set to connect to my android. ) Otherwise I used the Bluetooth function on my IPAD, IPOD and Nexus 4 (android phone) with no problem. *You can control the sound from your device or from the speaker. AND you can still pause your music using your device.
*Easy to charge. I really liked the fact that it is compatible with any USB or android charger. Meaning if you have an Apple device (ex., IPOD or IPAD), etc you can use the charger to charge this speaker. Or at least use the base portion of the charger. If you have an android, you can use that cord as well. The charge life for the battery is reasonable, and it even comes with a lithium battery.
*You can attach it to a book-bag or backpack (as shown in the photo), but I just place it where I want it to be and put it down. It is small enough (about the size of the palm of my hand) to fit into any purse, or bag without making it too heavy. Basically you can use this anywhere (in the home, camping, on trips, at the beach) and at any time.
* It's cute (I have the black. It kind of looks like a smashed soda can). Again, it's small. There are controls and indicator lights on the bottom of the device. The charge area is located on the top.

THINGS I WOULD CHANGE (not really a CON) about this product:
*The USB cord could be a bit longer. It was a little short for my tastes. But at least it's versatile.

So, as you can see, I was pleased with this product. The PROS definitely outweigh the "things that I would change" category. It had everything that made this a winner. It was easy to set up, and has decent sound quality. I definitely would recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches I wear headphones when I work outside, spring through fall. By the end of fall, that year’s pair is pretty nasty from hours of daily use and me sweating in them. Of course I clean them, but it’s impossible to *really* deep clean headphones.

So that’s what drew me to the adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones: the description advertises “removable, washable knitted ear cushions.” Knit covers I can wash? Hooray!

But there’s no instructions in the box on how to remove the ear covers or the headband. It turns out the cushions aren’t as removable as advertised.The ear cups twist off the headphones (a gentle, counter-clockwise turn), but there’s still an inner plastic rim. I thought I’d be able to wash the knitted cover itself, but nope. And I nearly tore the cover trying to figure out how to remove it, until I found the manual online.

I can’t figure out how to get the headband all the way off. The black plastic lining is removable, allowing the headband to be pushed up. I worry the headband will tear quickly, as the holes that line up with the black plastic lining aren’t reinforced.

Sound quality is okay … as long as I don’t use the Control Knob.

The Control Knob is like a volume rocker and skip/go back button in one. But when I used it to change the volume and skip tracks, I had static that lasted for several seconds.

There is an adidas Headphones app, but I thought it was useless. The only advantage of the app is that it allows you to set up to 3 customizable actions for the other button on the headphones. Oddly enough, at the time of writing this review, the app was only available on Android. I wanted to test the headphones on an iPhone too, but could not because the adidas Headphones app wasn’t available in my country (USA).

Lastly, the headphones are so uncomfortable to wear that I can’t wear them for more than 10 minutes. If I were inclined to use them, which I’m not, mainly because of the static whenever I use the Control Knob. I have a small head, but these headphones are tight and squeeze my ears and head. The ear cushions are actually quite scratchy too.
text_fidelity_b: adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches

This one has been one of my favorites to date, namely because it houses a SATA m.2 drive/SATA 2.5" ssd drive and has a built in ice cooler heatsink.

I've previously tried the Geekworm Pi NAS case and it was a smaller form factor case but it did not have any passive cooling for the Pi CPU. This Pro v2 case DOES. Driveway Alarm Wireless Outside, 1byone Motion Sensor Alarm 1000 FT Range Extra Loud Chimes Home Security Alarm System with 1 Receiver 2 Weatherproof Infrared Sensors Protect Indoor/Outdoor Property Today I removed the unit from my front steps where it has been since I first received it almost 2 years ago. It had been causing the indoor alarm unit to sound without ceasing. I removed the batteries to see what might be the problem, and I found ANTS had taken up residency inside the sensor unit. After clearing as many ants as possible, I put the unit in a plastic bag that is sealed. It will be several days before I open the unit to clean the circuit board as well as the housing. Then I will attempt to seal all openings so that I can use the sensor. It may not operate reliably once all the openings are sealed, but I have no other choice.

The second sensor is not giving me any problem because it is in a location that ants will not frequent.

As for locating the sensor in my mailbox so I will know when someone has opened the mailbox door, that won't work. The metal mailbox prevents a signal from being transmitted the 100 feet to the alarm. Also, ants like to use the mailbox which makes me spray an insecticide when I see them, and that's usually once a year.
text_fidelity_b: Driveway Alarm Wireless Outside, 1byone Motion Sensor Alarm 1000 FT Range Extra Loud Chimes Home Security Alarm System with 1 Receiver 2 Weatherproof Infrared Sensors Protect Indoor/Outdoor Property

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW), I own ALL of the kensington line of trackballs (clearly a trackball nut). From the original Expert Mouse (using a serial connection) all the way to this one. I can see how some purists are very touchy about their trackball performing and as it becomes an extension of interfacing with the computer, it's critical that it performs well.

PROS:
* Nice compact footprint; Not too demanding for space.
* Comes with the little ergonomic squishy thingy for a wrist-rest.
* The ball 'stays in' the unit even if you turn it over! This is a new concept for their trackballs! (you can pop it out if you need to condense for travel)
* Scroll wheel is nice; A feature present only in the higher-end trackballs.

CONS:
* BUTTONS! YUK! The button has some kind of contact issue where if you press it gently enough, you hear and feel a little 'click' but you didn't actuate the button! You must press it harder, and get a louder firmer CLICK! (really kinda mushy) to click it! I have tried different spots on the button and it's all the same! This is ALMOST a deal killer for me, but I'm going to give it some time, see if the button wears in and that false-click goes away over time.
* Scroll wheel is not free-flowing like on the modern expert mouse. With that sucker, you can fling the wheel and it will roll atleast for a half-second or so! This one really resists movement so it's more like a mouse-wheel than a scroll-wheel. It does not have a 'ribbed' feel, it rolls smoothly but it's not a 'on rails' as other models.

My personal favorite is still the modern expert mouse. It's massive (like a little tank on your desktop!) but you can navigate quickly with it, and use it in the manner a trackball was designed to be used.

Hope my review helps you!
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW),

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Back in 2016, I was getting into the Video Doorbells for extra security for packages. After much review of Ring, Skybell, Nest, and August doorbells, I decided to purchase the Skybell. I instantly enjoyed being able to get notifications when there was motion and when the button would be pressed. The advantage with Skybell was that it came with free subscription. Well... after 2 years of using the Skybell, i ran into many issues where the motion would not notify me or even pickup, wireless trying to connect to my network at home, and many other headaches which you would think be fixed after many patches. I have my own server room and network system which I ran network throughout my house and even have a business hotspot near the Skybell, still had many issues with the Skybell doorbell.

Moving forward......

I reviewed my options again as I was fed up with Skybell and still only had the same options today as they were 2 years ago. After much consideration i decided to choose the Ring Doorbell 2. They do offer a free subscription now, which is great, but you cannot review any motion or button press history events. Of course this is just due to needing to purchase the basic plan for the cloud storage. Even for $30 annually, the basic plan is still cost effective. After using the doorbell in the trial version of the plus plan, I am planning on paying the $30 just because its cheap cost and I would rather have the events to review rather than just seeing the live view.

Setup was easy (easier than Skybell). The app loads quick and can edit motion detection's, alerts, and much more. I connected the doorbell via hardwired to an analog doorbell. The box comes with many customization options, tools, and took only 10 minutes to install.

Testing the Ring doorbell worked perfectly and better than Skybell. I installed my Ring doorbell with the provided wedges that came in the box. I have a 20 foot driveway and the detection works so great that cars driving by alert me. You can decrease the range of the motion in the app. When there is motion, I can open the app from my lock-screen and only takes about 2 to 3 seconds before i can see the event. The load times are very quick and faster than Skybell.

Overall, I am day 15 in my trial and I am glad I decided on Ring. The product is great, and far better than competitors. Cost is ideal for those that do not want to pay hundreds each year on cloud storage like nest. I would highly recommend Ring to others.

text_fidelity_a: CozyPhones Sleep Headphones - Over Ear Headphones from Ultra Thin Cool Mesh Wired for Side Sleepers, Meditation, Running, Laptop, and Phone - Purple Lycra I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

ASUS Transformer Infinity TF700T Mobile Docking - Champagne I bought this at the same time I bought an Infinity TF700. I'm glad I did. I find screen touchpad typing difficult and I have pretty big hands. The keys on this are quite nice. Very good positive feel and comparable to most laptop keyboards. Complete set of Android function keys that cover just about everything. No need to be touching the screen. I wish the mouse pad was just a bit better. It's more than functional I guess. It's not bad, but it isn't great either. But I'm not a big fan of mouse pads anyway so I might be a bit over critical in this regard. .

The unit connects and disconnects nicely and has a lock lever which latches automatically. You can open it to about a 140 degree angle which makes getting a comforatble viewing angle possible in virtually any situation. If feels quite solid with no free play. Nice snug fit.

It gives you another battery too that adds 4.5 hours of uptime. You also get a standard sized USB 2.0 port and SD card reader. The USB port can operate in "host mode" allowing you to connect a variety of devices that should couple automatically. Can't say that I've used the USB a lot yet.

It is a very nice addition to a great tablet that gives you a laptop PC feel. It is tapered a little in thickness being a bit thicker at the back, but overall not much thicker than the tablet itself. Folded closed with the TF700 attached it's about 3/4 inch thick at the most and makes a nice sleek package. Connected together the two weigh right at 2.5 lbs.

The current price seems a bit high compared to other tablet's docking ports, but the keyboard is superior and the other features are quite nice. It's a worthwhile addition. I'd give it 5 stars if it were about $50 cheaper.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS Transformer Infinity TF700T Mobile Docking - Champagne

This thing performs as promised. I compared the pulse ox to another one that is placed on the fingers like traditional pulse ox. The 2 readings are within 1 to 2%.
I really like the sleep monitoring ability of this watch.
The watch syncs with my phone. I downloaded the app to my computer then sync my phone to the computer. I like that feature because I can see it better on a larger screen.
I do need to carry the phone with me when out walking the dog or the watch won't be able to sync and there will be missing data. I get notified on my watch when someone calls me. I get weather updates on the watch. I also get reminders to take a walk.
So my phone needs charging more often than normal.
I'm sold on smart watches now. I look forward to the newer watches coming out now more than ever.

Jabra Stealth Bluetooth Headset - Black (US Version) I am pleased with this headset; the sound quality is good and audibility is very sharp. The music quality is also good. Assembly is very simple and needs no additional tools to set it together. It also fits well into my ears. I have been using this set for the last three weeks and it works great. It is paired with my cell phone and I use this to listen to the incoming calls and also listen to the music from micro SD card inserted into the cell phone. It is small and has a discreet design. It is very light, easy to carry and works great. The gadget also synchronizes easily with phone, but it does not pair with my Garmin Nuvi GPS machine or my Acer Chromebook both of which are Bluetooth-enabled.

Pairing with cell phone is very easy; just turn the headset on and the cell phone on, it detects the Bluetooth easily and within a minute it gives the message that it is paired. The built-in battery is excellent, and on one charge it lasts for about 5-6 hours of use time. The downside is that this piece doesn't have a separate mute button or the volume button; you have to control volume from your cell phone. Another negative feature is that the three replacement parts for earpiece that comes with the set are of same size, hence gives little option for someone with small (or large) ears. I have rated this product four stars for overall satisfaction.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Stealth Bluetooth Headset - Black (US Version)

text_fidelity_a:
HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year) I was really looking forward to trying this tablet out. To date I'd had no exposure to Windows 8.1 or a dedicated Windows tablet. I have had a decent 10.1 inch Android tablet.

First are foremost, the elephant in the room... or rather, the mouse. This is a seven inch wide screen tablet. I have friends whose who online lives are conducted via five inch cell phone screens and they're happy with it. The screen on this tablet is nice. Don't get me wrong. I was able to stream from Amazon video in HD (720) and the video was crisp and clean. Images display well but, again, the screen is just seven inches. I can't imagine trying to be productive with something so small.

For a device with only one gig of RAM this runs Windows fairly well. I wws able to load several Windows programs including the Calibrě eBook manager which took a little longer to convert eBooks between formats but did the job. I also loaded a legacy email and Usenet program that I've been using for a decade or longer. Along with directly installed programs I also downloaded a handful of apps from the very buggy Microsoft app store. The store worked less than 50% of the time while I was trying this tablet out. I at one point had to resort to switching to a local login account and then back to my Hotmail logi. It only took about an hour of reading web forums to find that solution to the Windows app store refusing to work.

Two problems I ran into were the sound which is from a single speaker hidden in a slot on one of the short sides of the tablet. If you want to listen to anything other than the default Window's beeps and tones you'll want to pair this with a blue tooth speaker or headphones. The speaker in this tablet is deplorable. The next problem I had was the tablet runs HOT. I was running a program designed for Windows 98, downloading and reading posts un Usenet and viewing a few posted vacation and astronomy images and I had to stop. The tablet was so hot it was uncomfortable to hold and I worried it might overheat and become damaged.

While I was impressed to see Windows running on a small tablet I was thoroughly unimpressed with Windows 8.1 the tile system is just terrible.

So, it has good video quality on a too small screen with horrible sound and a flaky app store to rely upon, though you can download and install normal Windows programs. I just wasn't that crazy about this tablet. And will definitely be sticking with Android and a much larger screen.
text_fidelity_b: HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year)

Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 The mouse functions fine and I do like the form of it. There is one critical problem though. The form forces the forward and back buttons to be on the opposite side of left and right click so while your thumb is on the forward or back, you have no choice but to squeeze the right or left click to engage the forward/back button. Obviously, this causes inadvertent clicks with the mouse which is a problem. It happens mainly on the forward button as this is where the left and right click start to engage, too (more forward on the mouse itself).

I have not decided if I will keep it or not as I rely heavily on the use of these buttons. If I can find a way to grip it so this does not occur, it will be fine. In the meantime, I'll be using it look for a mouse that is designed better.

UPDATE 2-23-16: Like many others who have posted less than favorable reviews, Anker customer support has reached out to me directly, twice, offering a full refund, which I declined. In my opinion, the mouse works well for it's price, but I stand by the issue noted above. I have gotten used to is and can grip the mouse slightly differently when using the forward button. For this reason and for the outstanding customer service, I have bumped the review to 3 stars and wouldn't hesitate to recommend trying it out given the extremely low risk.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod, Black The Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod is basically (pardon the pun) everything you need in a monopod. It extends to a nice height and even at full extension it feels reasonably sturdy. Collapsing the thinnest section and using just the two thicker sections increases the stability greatly and still gives you a little over 51 inches to work with.

Build quality is decent. The locking cams are hard plastic but don't feel cheap and give a positive, tight lock when engaged. The foam grip isn't glued into place. It is just held in place by friction and the three screw heads that hold the camera mount to the monopod.

The monopod also includes a wrist strap held in place on the head of the mount by a split ring.

A carry bag is supplied. It's enough to protect the monopod though it's not padded and the shoulder strap is short enough to be more of a carry strap.

The rubber foot of this monopod can be retracted on its threaded mount to expose a metal spike foot for use in outdoor.

The only negatives I've found with this monopod are:
The wrist strap is rather small and I cannot fit it over my hand. For reference I wear a size large glove. For me this is more of a palm strap.

Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black As an avid fan of Alexa, I am delighted to have this Harman Kardon Alexa speaker. I've had my original Echo since the first week they released the initial invitation to buy and have since added a Dot and Alexa controlled thermostats, dining room lights, Fire TV sticks and plugs through out the house. This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.
text_fidelity_b: Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black

Single Monitor Arm Mount | Desk Stand | Heavy Duty Full Motion Height Adjustable | Fits 19 21 24 27 29 30 in VESA 75 100 Compatible Computer Screen | C-Clamp Base | Holds up to 33 Lbs I purchased this specifically to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]]. It definitely holds the monitor - steady - in any position within this mount's range. Note that my monitor weighs in around 9.5 pounds, so factor that into your own needs.

Assembly is a snap. It comes with everything you need to mount the VESA adapter to your monitor, including washers and spacers. I had anticipated having to purchase bolts to fit, but that turned out to be unnecessary.

One of the things I love is the VESA bracket has slots that fit into horizontal posts. Those support the full weight of the monitor while you are installing the two adjustment bolts. In other words, assembling, mounting and adjusting this can be done by one person. My mount shipped with thumb style bolts and optional, heavier ones that you can use with the included hex wrench. Since my monitor was so light to begin with I used the thumb bolts, which hold the viewing angle in the narrow range of movement the VESA mount allows. Had my monitor been heavier I would have probably used the hex bolts, which are a lot beefier.

Bottom line: read some of the other reviews that discuss challenges that this mount has for heavier and larger monitors. However, if you have a 24" that is in the 10-12 pound range (or less) this is all the mount that you need. It's built like a tank, is a breeze to assemble, and holds lighter monitors absolutely rock steady.

text_fidelity_a:
Olympus OM-D E-M1 16MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3-Inch LCD (Body Only) (Silver w/ Black Trim) I have been shooting Olympus cameras since 1978. I have always loved the lenses. With over 2,000,000 shots on my Olympus E-500 camera, I decided it was time to invest in a new camera.

I was reluctant at first to try the EM-1 for three reasons:
- The format is Micro-Four Thirds, not Four Thirds. I take 99% of my photos in the telephoto range, and that is what Four Thirds was optimized to use. Micro-Four Thirds is geared more towards wide angle lenses.
- The camera is mirrorless and uses an electronic Viewfinder (EVF).
- I have to use a converter to mount my existing Four Thirds lenses, and converters have a very bad history.

Out of the box:
The first thing that you notice when you pull the body out is that it is SOLID. The thing feels like it is built like a tank. I have not tried the "splashproof" and other claims, but just holding this body I can believe them. The camera fits well in my hand. My hands are a little large, and my pinky occasionally slides off the bottom. I may buy the grip/extra battery holder later if this proves to be a problem. YMMV.

Using Four Thirds lenses:
I have no Micro Four Thirds lenses and a lot invested in Four Thirds lenses, so using them was a key issue. Olympus has 1/17 or 1 MP of the sensor dedicated to phase detection auto focus, the only type of auto focus that will work with these lenses. I find that the system works very well. Focusing is fast and accurate.

Mounting the converter is easy, as expected. Once mounted, you use a button on the side to release the lens. This is a learning issue since I still normally hit the lens release button on the camera body. I anticipate little real problems with this since as soon as I try to put the cover on the back of the lens I realize my error.

Balance with the 12-60 mm Four Thirds lens is excellent. Holding the lens by the zoom collar, the weight is only slightly behind my left hand. I only have to support the body lightly with my right hand. I personally like that balance. Longer lenses like the 70-300 are also well balanced.

EVF:
I have used a mirrored SLR since 1978 and a rangefinder 35 mm camera and 126 film P&S cameras before that. As you might guess, I favor a direct view to see what I am shooting. EVF have issues with resolution and lag when moving to a different point of interest or following a subject, especially in low light.

The EVF has turned out to be great. I really like Olympus' implementation. There is some lag, but it is generally minimal. The "What You See Is What You Get" is a big plus in my book. Adjust the exposure compensation or manual exposure settings, and the view in the EVF changes to reflect what the image will look like. It is not perfect, but it gets 95%+ of what you will actually get. The display of settings is bright, clear, crisp, large, and surprisingly unobtrusive.

The EVF also allows a lot of changes in camera settings to be done without removing the camera from your eye. Use the two dials, and you can see where the focus points that you are using are. Hit the OK button on the back, and you can use the dials to adjust just about every setting while watching the selections you are making in the EVF. Ditto with the other buttons like HDR and auto exposure mode.

HDR:
I had the opportunity to use in-camera HDR while on a recent trip. The day was cloudy, and there was a lot of shadow against bright grey clouds. The in-camera HDR used a series of shots at different exposures and combined them in the camera. The results were better than HDR Pro in Photoshop CS5.5 IMO. I was much, much happier with the dynamic range and overall look of the images. the 10 fps shooting mode was also great for minimizing camera movement, ghosts and other problems associated with HDR.

Image stabilization:
The EM-1 has a five axis image stabilization system for the sensor. That means any lens becomes can be used. The fourth and fifth axes are for rotations. One compensates for the slight turn of the camera that often occurs when you press the shutter button. I had good success using IS in low light with my 70-300 mm lens set at 300 mm.

Scenes:
the EM-1 has many useful scene modes. I used landscape and panorama with great success. The artistic filters and story modes may also interest you. I prefer to do those types of things in post-processing.

ISO:
The camera has an almost insane 25600 maximum ISO. Yes, you get image quality degradation and noise at that ISO, but the in-camera JPEG processor can actually give you some relief from the problems at higher ISOs. I so far have found shooting up to ISO 1600 produces no discerned degradation. I tried ISO 6400 and found minimal issues.

For those who started with film and were in love with the "high ISO" 1000 film for low light shooting, this is a major and welcome advancement. For those newer to photography that have been using higher ISO cameras for a while, the speed may not be much of a gain, but the image quality should be.

The low end ISO is 200, which is the new normal. I do not find it to be a problem. I would rather shoot at a faster shutter speed than have an ISO 100 setting in most cases. There is an ISO LOW setting, but I do not plan to use it. If you regularly shoot in bright light and want lower f-stops, invest in a neutral density filter.

Back display:
The back display is slightly disappointing. It can only tilt up and down, not rotate so that you can see your composition when you are getting into the shot. It works well for shooting over crowds or getting a low angle shot.

On the plus side, the display is clear, bright and a touchscreen that can be used to select a point of interest for focusing and can be used to take the shot in live view mode. You can also use it to select settings to change. The next generation should be even better, and hopefully it will have a screen that rotates.

SD card:
One change from the E-500 that I do not like is the use of SD rather than CF cards. CF cards are nearly indestructible, and a good Sansdisk Extreme card works virtually anywhere, anytime and is virtually impossible to physically break. The xD card slot disappearing is no loss, but not having a second card slot is somewhat surprising given the high-end prosumer/professional positioning of this camera.

Controls and customization:
The controls are pretty well placed for me with the exception of the auto exposure lock button. That is right beside the viewfinder and too far to the left for my liking. You can do a lot of customization with the control buttons and dials, but there are limits. I have not made any changes yet because I am still learning the camera. Overall the defaults seem logical and useful.

This camera has two dials, one on the front and one on the back. The E-500 only had a back dial, so I am learning to use the two dial system. They work well for adjusting and selecting options. I think the second dial was a good addition. Both are conveniently located for my fingers.

Image quality:
All of this is meaningless if the image you get out is bad. The EM-1 does not disappoint. I know that there are people who insist that they need 48 MP or some other ridiculously large number. The reality is that 16 MP is a great size for printing full-size 300 dpi images on your printer or using a commercial photo printing service. If all you do is screen displays, it is about eight times more pixels than you need for a typical 2 MP monitor.

The quality of the EM-1 pixels is very high, and you get excellent out-of-the-camera RAW and JPEG images. I have no problems seeing fine detail at 100% and higher magnifications.

Summary:
This camera is a winner, and it works with my existing Four Thirds lenses so I do not have to invest another $3000+ in lenses to use it. text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix T300 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens (Black) For the non-professional photographer looking to get high-quality images in a variety of settings, this camera works great. I did a little experiment to see how it performed by taking it with me to Europe along with a much more expensive semi-professional Nikon (D3100). Here are the results:

Advantages:
-With our limited time, my camera was able to take a variety of shots (panoramic, zoom, close-up) quickly and easily while the Nikon could only take limited kinds because of the need to bring several lenses and because of the complexity (sometimes) of setting up a given shot
-Because it was small, I didn't have to lug around a big camera bag, which also had the potential of getting a little too much unwanted attention
-One feature I really enjoyed was the two simultaneous flash/no flash shot which gives you the same picture with and without flash, letting you choose later which you prefer
-Didn't need more than one lens
-With city shots of architecture, my camera fared better with its versatility

Disadvantages:
-In the mountains, the Nikon did better, capturing color and clarity/detail. In my shots, the trees looked less defined from high up. Also, his zoom lens was able to capture much more detail than my camera.
-Nature shots and portraits have slightly duller colors, missing something the other camera was able to capture
-There was slightly more blur in shots with movement with this camera

Conclusion:
For the price, this camera performed much better than I expected and was not as much of a hassle as our semi-professional camera, so for most people, this is not only going to be a better value, but less frustrating and cumbersome. For the professional, this is obviously not the best choice, but this isn't being marketed as a professional camera. This is a great family and vacation camera that everyone can use, and that still yields quality images with plenty of artistic integrity.
Great little camera, and fun to use!

**see pics for some examples of how this camera performed**
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix T300 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding I'm having a serious problem with the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base that apparently the other reviewers are not having. I called Denon Technical Support and after spending a lot of time behind the TV set making sure all the wires were hooked up correctly and then pressing different buttons on the Denon Speaker base, they can't figure out what is causing this problem. And the problem is this: No sound signal is going to the Denon speaker base through the TV from the Roku player. The Roku works just fine through the regular TV speakers and is connected directly to the TV via HDMI. When the input on the TV is set to stream via the Roku no sound comes through the Denon and it turns off. If I increase the volume on the TV speakers you hear sound. If the input is changed to TV with the TV sound off, sound will come through the Denon. Also, if a DVD is played on the DVD player which is connected to the TV, the sound comes through the Denon. It just won't put out sound when the Roku input is being used. And that's a real bummer for me because we watch a lot of Netflix and Amazon streaming through our Roku. I am using the digital optical cord included with the Denon Speaker Base. I have it connected to the Digital Optical "Out" on the back of my Sharp 37" flat screen TV to the digital optical "In" on the back of the Denon Speaker Base.

I will keep working on this problem, and if anyone reading this has any idea that might fix it please say so in the comments section. I would love very much to have it work and to raise the star level to 5. When sound does come through the Denon it's great! Loud, clear and no buzzes or rattles whatsoever like when the volume is turned all the way up when using the TV speakers. I love that it can get loud and there's no rattles or weird vibrations. and the night mode is very useful since the TV room is located underneath the main bedroom and my husband has to go to bed early since he has to go to work early. I like to stay up late and watch Netflix/Amazon or other streaming channels through the Roku (oops! That doesn't work through the Denon) and I keep the volume down lest it wake him up. I was really looking forward to using the Denon night sound function.

The Denon tech suggested hooking everything up to another TV to see if the problem is the Roku player or my TV. Unfortunately, I don't have another TV to test out the units to try and isolate the lack of sound from the Roku player to the Denon. I was really wanting to use this for night listening, but since I can't I will take the Denon to my mom's nursing home and hook it up to her small, flat-screen TV. Since she's half deaf, it might can help her hear the sound better. I will update this review afterwards.
text_fidelity_b: Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity Just spent a week and a half in hospital. After dithering for a couple of weeks, I finally took the plunge and ordered the kindle the day before surgery. I had a small satchel (guy purse) to carry wallet, kindle and phone with me when in therapy. My arms were too weak to hold the book I had with me. Friends brought my kindle to me the 3rd day. I then read about 5 to 6 hours or more a day and night. Charging was fast and I had no issues with battery life. I charged once a day. If needed I could read while kindle was charging. I bought the 3g and wi-fi addition. Downloaded on both as hospital wi-fi quit sometimes at night. Holding a book to read had become a chore for me some years ago. Sitting at a table reading was uncomfortable, therefore I have neglected to my reading. I have downloaded Edgar A. Poe's works. I especially enjoy his comic and scientific pieces. (See high school English classes ruined Poe for you, didn't it? It did for me until I discovered his other writings.) I downloaded some other large and heavy in print books. I am angry at self for not discovering the kindle and amazon book experience before now. I own some 3,000 volumes of history, science, etc. Very little fiction, except for Poe, Shakespeare, Twain, Doyle, and their ilk interests me. I don't read popular novels at all. I was surprised at the number of books and editions available for free or almost free that covers my interests. I don't consider myself as a snob for not liking popular fiction, it just doesn't interest me. But reading is a mind expanding activity, whatever one reads. It doesn't matter what you read, just do it.
I am 77 years old new kindle reader. Thanks amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I have a Nuvi 360. It came with a suction cup windshield mount. It also came with a steel disk with double sticky adhesive on the back. I was supposed to mount this disk somewhere on my dashboard, then use the suction cup to attach the mount. I didn't want to use the suction mount directly onto the windshield because 1) it telegraphs the presence of an expensive GPS unit, 2) it's illegal in California to attach anything to the windshield and 3) I don't think the suction cup would last very long.

Then there's the disk with the very permanent double sticky tape. The problem with almost all cars these days is there really isn't anywhere to attach the disk discreetly. Every square inch is taken with existing stuff. And who wants an ugly disk glued to the dash anyway? And what if I want to use the GPS in other vehicles? More disks?

So I settled on this "beanbag" mount with the ball mount arm.

Unfortunately, before the beanbag friction mount arrived, I was flexing the arm in the suction cup mount and noticed the suction cup's mounting bracket had already broken. I had never even attached it to anything! The mount is beautifully engineered and built...except for one area where the arm's hinge pin attaches to the suction cup's plastic hinge loops. The loops are too thin and fragile. The loops cracked and broke with hardly any hinging at all.

So now I have a quite useless suction mount but a very functional ball arm. What to do?

I drove the hinge pin out of the ball arm. Then I took two small 1" x 1" steel angle brackets and attached them to the ball arm with a 2" long, 8-32 threaded machine screw and an 8-32 wingnut. This created two "feet" for the ball arm. Then I epoxied the two bracket "feet" to the fabric (upper) side of an old 1/4" thick mousepad. Ta da. A friction pad for pennies with a ball arm attached.

Works great. Cost was virtually nothing. Doesn't slide on either of the two dashboards I've tried it on. The mousepad is flexible and conforms easily to the curving shape of the various dashboards. It doesn't weigh much but the thick mousepad has enough heft to plant the getup nicely. The grippy rubber side of the mousepad adheres nicely to the dash. Yet I can pull it down to the floor quickly and reposition it easily.

I wish I'd thought of this BEFORE I ordered this "official" friction mount to the tune of a couple of twenties.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging
